confirmed.title: Live SOCSO employee rate is 0.5% — Settings default contradicts rates.py 1.25% (R3)
confirmed.evidence: models.py:37 `socso_c1_emp: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(RATE, default=Decimal("0.005"))` vs core/rates.py:14 `SOCSO_C1_EMP = Decimal("0.0125")` (R3: employee 1.25% eff. 1 Jun 2026, Employer Circular 2/2026). All live compute paths use store.rate_config(db) (store.py:35-38), which builds RateConfig from the Settings row that get_settings() creates with the model default 0.005. Verified: RateConfig(socso_c1_emp=0.005) → SOCSO employee RM24.75 on a RM5,000 wage; DEFAULT_CONFIG → RM61.90. Every Category-1 employee in the running app is under-deducted 0.75pp of SOCSO, violating R3 and the §1 core guarantee. Migration 0001 defines settings.socso_c1_emp NOT NULL with no default, so existing deployed rows also hold 0.005.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Decide the authoritative rate (per domain R3: 0.0125), change the Settings model default to Decimal("0.0125"), and ship a data migration `update settings set socso_c1_emp = 0.0125 where socso_c1_emp = 0.005;`. Add a startup assertion (or test) that the Settings row's statutory rates match rates.py defaults unless deliberately overridden, and reconcile domain W1 which still encodes the 0.5% figure.

confirmed.title: Statutory self-test fails against current rates and is the engine's only guard
confirmed.evidence: `assert (r.socso_employee, r.socso_employer) == (Decimal("24.75"), Decimal("86.65")), r` — running `python -m app.statutory` raises AssertionError: actual socso_employee=61.90, net_salary=4268.20 with DEFAULT_CONFIG (0.0125). Lines 116-118 (24.75 / 4305.35) encode the old 0.5% rate. There is no tests/ directory anywhere in backend/ (verified with find), so this failing __main__ block is the only executable check on the money engine — and domain L1 records that EPF/SOCSO already regressed once (git 587d436). CLAUDE.md mandates pytest tests for every function.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Update the expected figures to the current rates (socso_employee 61.90, total_employee_deduction 731.80, net 4268.20; keep employer 86.65 / cost 5746.55), then port W1–W3 plus band-edge cases (RM30/50/70/100/140/200, RM5,000/5,000.01, RM6,000 ceiling, over_60, foreign) into backend/tests/test_statutory.py run in CI/Make, computing with both DEFAULT_CONFIG and a Settings-derived RateConfig.

confirmed.title: EPF uses RM20 bands for all wages; Third Schedule uses RM100 bands above RM5,000
confirmed.evidence: `BAND_WIDTH = Decimal("20")` and band_upper() applies it to every wage. The official KWSP Third Schedule tabulates RM20 bands only up to RM5,000; above that the bands are RM100 wide (and above RM20,000 the rate applies to the exact wage). Verified: wage RM5,050 → code gives (557, 608); the official schedule row RM5,000.01–5,100 gives 11%×5,100=561 / 12%×5,100=612. EPF is understated for every employee earning over RM5,000 whose wage isn't at a RM100 band top. Domain R2's verification rows (RM2,550/3,350/5,000) are all ≤ RM5,000, so the >5,000 region was never checked.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In band_upper(), use RM100 band width when wage > RM5,000 (band = ceil(w/100)*100) and, above RM20,000, apply the rate to the exact wage rounded up per the schedule. Verify against official rows above RM5,000 (e.g. RM5,050, RM7,777) and add them to the tests; update domain R2.

confirmed.title: Age-60 cutoff evaluated on the 1st of the run month, never re-derived, silently false without DOB
confirmed.evidence: `period = dt.date(run.year, run.month, 1); age = emp.age_on(period); ... over_60=bool(age is not None and age >= 60)`. An employee turning 60 on the 15th of the run month has age 59 on the 1st → charged Category 1 employee SOCSO plus EIS for that month, while PERKESO applies Category 2 (and stops EIS) from the month of the 60th birthday. models.py:143-147 age_on returns None when dob is missing → over_60 defaults False with no warning. The flag is derived once at slip creation and recompute()/run_save never re-derive it from dob (FLAG_FIELDS makes it manually flippable), so a dob correction leaves a stale category. This is exactly domain H4/OPEN-2.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Derive over_60 from age at month end (or explicitly: turns 60 at any point on/before the run month's last day → Category 2), re-derive it from Employee.dob inside run_save/recompute instead of trusting the stored flag, and surface a review warning when dob is missing for an employee with SOCSO/EIS enabled. Document the chosen cutoff in domain statutory.md (resolves OPEN-2).

confirmed.title: SOCSO/EIS band table missing the 100–140 and 140–200 sub-bands
confirmed.evidence: `edges = [0, 30, 50, 70] + list(range(100, int(ceiling) + 1, 100))` treats RM100.01–200 as one band with midpoint 150. The official PERKESO/EIS schedule has separate bands >RM100–140 (assumed wage 120) and >RM140–200 (assumed wage 170). Verified: band_midpoint(120) → 150 (official 120, so a RM120 earner is over-deducted: 1.90 vs 1.50 employee) and band_midpoint(170) → 150 (official 170, under-deducted). Only affects confirmed staff earning ≤ RM200/month, so real exposure is small, but it is a band-edge defect of the H3 class.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Change the low-band edges to `[0, 30, 50, 70, 100, 140, 200]` before the RM100 bands starting at 200, and add band-edge tests at 100/100.01/140/140.01/200/200.01.

confirmed.title: Run population ignores blocker/verified-bank exclusion and the period window
confirmed.evidence: sync_new_employees/available_employees select `Employee.active.is_(True)` only (payroll.py:165-167, 181-183). The blocked-from-payroll rule (runs-and-exports R2: open blocker flag or unverified bank → excluded) is enforced only in payroll_master_view (0004_views.sql:36-41) for the CSV, not in the payroll-run builder; and there is no hire_date/last_working_day window (R3), so a leaver from a prior month still marked active, or someone hired after period end, gets a full payslip. Worse, _new_payslip snapshots `bank_account=emp.bank_account` (payroll.py:67) — the raw employees column, not the verified bank_accounts row — so an unverified account can flow onto an approved payslip and the dashboard's by-bank payment totals, directly against the §1 guarantee.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In sync_new_employees/available_employees/add_employee, apply the same predicate as payroll_master_view (status='active', no open blocker flag, verified bank account exists, hire_date ≤ period end, last_working_day null or ≥ period start) — e.g. select employee ids from payroll_master_view for the run's period — and snapshot bank details from the verified bank_accounts row. Surface excluded employees in the run UI as 'blocked from payroll'.

confirmed.title: No unique constraint on payslips (run_id, employee_id) — duplicate payslips possible
confirmed.evidence: Payslip defines only `run_id ... index=True` and `employee_id ... index=True`; migration 0001 creates plain indexes (lines 142-143), no UNIQUE. Duplicate protection is in-Python only: add_employee checks `any(s.employee_id == employee_id for s in run.payslips)` and sync_new_employees a `have` set before commit (payroll.py:151, 164). Two concurrent /sync or add-slip requests (or a retried request) can both pass the check and insert two payslips for the same employee — double pay in totals, exports and PDFs. This is hazard H3 (idempotency of run compute).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `UniqueConstraint("run_id", "employee_id", name="uq_payslip_run_employee")` to Payslip.__table_args__ plus a migration `create unique index ... on payslips (run_id, employee_id)` (dedupe first), and catch IntegrityError in add_employee/sync_new_employees to treat the duplicate as already-present.

confirmed.title: No proration for mid-month joiners/leavers; work_days_default never used in computation
confirmed.evidence: _new_payslip sets `basic=Decimal("0") if is_part else (emp.basic_salary or 0)` — the full monthly basic regardless of hire_date or last_working_day inside the run month; statutory.compute has no proration path. `work_days_default` is stored on the run (payroll.py:140-141) but never read by any calculation, so a joiner on the 20th or a leaver on the 5th is paid a full month unless the clerk manually notices and flips count_by_day with hand-keyed units. Runs-and-exports H1 names month-boundary proration a confirmed hazard; nothing in the engine or run builder addresses it.
confirmed.proposed_fix: When hire_date or last_working_day falls inside the run month, default the slip to count_by_day with units = worked days (per the company's chosen convention, e.g. calendar-day or work_days_default proportion) and rate = basic/work_days_default, and flag the slip for review. At minimum, warn on slips whose employee has a mid-month hire/LWD.

confirmed.title: Movements view labels every leaver 'hire_and_leave' — classification ignores dates' month
confirmed.evidence: `case when e.hire_date is not null and e.last_working_day is not null then 'hire_and_leave' when e.last_working_day is not null then 'leaver' else 'new_hire' end` — the movement type tests only NULL-ness. Every employee has a hire_date on record, so any leaver (hired years ago, LWD this month) is exported as 'hire_and_leave'; 'leaver' is only reachable when hire_date is NULL. The movements CSV (payroll_export.py:53-67) filters rows to the month but passes this mislabel straight to the clerk who uses it for final-pay handling.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Classify per exported month: since the endpoint knows year/month, compute movement in the query (hire_date within month AND lwd within month → 'hire_and_leave'; only lwd within month → 'leaver'; only hire_date within month → 'new_hire'), or expose both dates and derive the label in payroll_export.py instead of the view.

confirmed.title: Money inputs accept negatives and silently coerce garbage to 0
confirmed.evidence: `def _dec(raw, default="0"): try: return Decimal(str(raw)...) except (InvalidOperation, AttributeError): return Decimal(default)` — invalid input becomes 0 with no 422, and negative values pass through. run_save (main.py:270-278) writes these directly into basic/rate/units/allowance/deduction/ot_hours/ot_rate/pcb_override and recomputes: a posted negative allowance or negative pcb_override silently distorts net salary and statutory wage; a typo like '1,2o0' becomes RM0 basic and zeroes the whole payslip without any error. CLAUDE.md mandates input validation; this is a §6 money path.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In run_save, reject non-parseable values with 422 (don't default to 0) and enforce field-appropriate ranges: basic/rate/units/allowance/ot_hours/ot_rate/pcb_override ≥ 0, deduction ≥ 0, with sensible upper bounds. Return per-field errors so the UI can highlight the offending cell.

confirmed.title: Payslip PDF omits the LINDUNG deduction line while its total includes it
confirmed.evidence: pdf.py:91-96 itemizes only EPF/SOCSO/EIS/PCB and the 'other' deduction, but recompute (payroll.py:46-48) does `slip.total_employee_deduction += slip.lindung_amount; slip.net_salary -= slip.lindung_amount`. As soon as an admin sets a non-zero lindung_24jam_rate for an opted-in employee, the printed 'Total deductions' will not equal the sum of the listed rows and net won't reconcile on the employee-facing document. Latent today only because the default rate is RM0.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In payslip_pdf, append `("LINDUNG 24Jam", slip.lindung_amount)` to the deductions list when slip.lindung_optin and lindung_amount > 0 (and add the column to run_summary_pdf if material).

confirmed.title: default_include_allowance / default_include_ot settings are dead — hardcoded True/False override them
confirmed.evidence: _new_payslip hardcodes `include_allowance=True, include_ot=False` (payroll.py:74-75) and run_save re-forces `slip.include_allowance = True; slip.include_ot = False` on every save (main.py:294-295). Yet Settings.default_include_allowance/default_include_ot are exposed in the admin settings API (serializers.py:14, main.py:423) — grep shows no other reader. An admin toggling statutory-wage composition (rule R1's opt-in) sees the setting saved but it has zero effect, misleading on a money-relevant control.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either wire the two settings into _new_payslip/run_save in place of the hardcoded values, or (if 'basic + allowance always, OT never' is fixed company policy per the code comments) remove them from SETTINGS_FIELDS/SETTING_KINDS and the UI, and record the policy as a DECISION in the domain file.

confirmed.title: Preparer can edit payslip figures while the run is pending approval
confirmed.evidence: editable_by: `if self.status == "pending": return bool(user and (user.can_approve or user.can_prepare))` — run_save (main.py:261) therefore lets the preparer keep changing amounts after submitting for approval, with no re-submission or approver-visible change marker; the approver may approve figures that changed since they started reviewing. The docstring ('Preparer edits draft/rejected; approver may also edit while pending') reads as approver-only for pending.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Restrict pending-state edits to approvers (`return bool(user and user.can_approve)`), or force any pending-state edit to bounce the run back to draft/require re-submission, so approval always covers the exact stored figures.

confirmed.title: Payroll tables store Numeric(12,2) ringgit, contradicting the confirmed integer-sen storage rule
confirmed.evidence: `MONEY = Numeric(12, 2)` and every payslip/settings money column in migration 0001 is NUMERIC(12,2) ringgit, while PROJECT_PROFILE §3 and runs-and-exports R4 [confirmed] state 'Money stored as integer sen; views/exports convert at the edge' — only the employee-master tables (0002: basic_salary_sen integer) follow it. NUMERIC(12,2) is still exact (no float hazard; the sen views cast `(e.basic_salary * 100)::integer` correctly), but the codebase now has two money conventions and the documented rule is false for the entire payroll engine's persistence.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either migrate payslip/settings money columns to integer sen with edge conversion (large change; schedule outside the month-end window), or amend R4/PROJECT_PROFILE to state the actual rule ('exact NUMERIC(12,2) ringgit in payroll tables, integer sen in employee-master and export views') so future agents don't 'fix' code against a wrong rule.

confirmed.title: Forgeable sessions: hardcoded default session-signing secret with no production guard
confirmed.evidence: config.py:16 `SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("PAYROLL_SECRET", "onni-payroll-dev-secret-change-me")`; docker-compose.yml:22 `PAYROLL_SECRET: ${PAYROLL_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}`; main.py:29 `app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=SECRET_KEY, max_age=60 * 60 * 12)`. Starlette SessionMiddleware cookies are itsdangerous-signed client-side tokens. With the publicly known default secret (it is in the git repo), anyone who can reach the API can mint a cookie containing {"user_id": <admin id>} and become admin without credentials — full access to NRIC, bank accounts, salaries, and run approval. Nothing refuses to boot when the default secret is in use.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Fail fast at startup when PAYROLL_SECRET is unset or equals a known default (e.g. in config.py: raise RuntimeError unless APP_ENV=development). Remove the compose fallback default so `docker compose up` without a .env refuses to start rather than running with a forgeable key. Rotate the secret on any deployed instance.

confirmed.title: payroll_master_view (NRIC, bank account, salary) likely readable via Supabase anon key — RLS bypassed by security-definer views created after the revoke
confirmed.evidence: 0003_rls.sql:25 revokes only what existed then: `revoke all on all tables in schema public from anon, authenticated;`. 0004_views.sql then does `create or replace view payroll_master_view as select ... e.nric as identity_no, ... (e.basic_salary * 100)::integer as basic_salary_sen, ... ba.bank_name, ba.account_no ...` with no revoke/grant statements and no `security_invoker`. On Supabase, ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants SELECT on newly created objects in `public` to anon/authenticated, and Postgres views default to security-definer semantics (run as the view owner), so the tables' RLS does not apply through the view. Result: the PostgREST anon key can read every active employee's NRIC, salary, and verified bank account. supabase/rls_test.sql (lines 6-20) only tests base tables, never the three views, so the gap is invisible to the existing 'RLS proof'.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a migration: `alter view payroll_master_view set (security_invoker = true);` (same for payroll_blocked_view, payroll_movements_view), plus `revoke all on payroll_master_view, payroll_blocked_view, payroll_movements_view from anon, authenticated;` and consider `alter default privileges in schema public revoke select on tables from anon, authenticated;` so future objects are safe. Extend supabase/rls_test.sql to select from all three views as anon/authenticated and require 0 rows / permission denied.

confirmed.title: Default weak credentials (admin/admin123) force-reset on every container start, no password change path, no login rate limiting
confirmed.evidence: config.py:20-30 seeds `"password": os.environ.get("ADMIN_PASS", "admin123")` (and preparer123/approver123). backend/Dockerfile:12 `CMD ["sh", "-c", "python seed.py && uvicorn ..."]` runs seed.py on every start, and seed.py:75-84 `seed_users` OVERWRITES the stored hash: `user.password_hash = hash_password(spec["password"])` — so even a manually changed password reverts on restart; there is no change-password endpoint anywhere in the API. Makefile:8 prints the credentials: `@echo "Demo accounts: preparer/preparer123 · approver/approver123 · admin/admin123"`. main.py:71-79 login has no rate limiting, lockout, or delay, so the three fixed usernames are trivially brute-forceable even with changed passwords.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Require *_PASS env vars (refuse to boot with defaults outside dev), make seed_users create-if-missing only (never overwrite an existing hash), add a password-change endpoint, and add per-IP/per-username throttling (e.g. slowapi) plus a constant-time failure delay on /api/auth/login. Remove credentials from Makefile output.

confirmed.title: Anonymous IDOR: predictable reference numbers let anyone overwrite documents of any employee, including active staff
confirmed.evidence: registration.py:171-181 `/api/register/{ref}/documents/{doc_type}` is unauthenticated and only checks `select employee_id from application_submissions where reference_no = :r` — with no check that the employee is still an applicant. Legacy imports create fully predictable refs (import_legacy_form.py:268 `ref = f"GF-{r:03d}"`, i.e. GF-001, GF-002 …) that map to now-ACTIVE employees. storage.py:41 uploads with `"x-upsert": "true"`, so an anonymous attacker can permanently overwrite an active employee's stored NRIC/work-permit/food-handler images at `applicants/<ref>/<doc_type>.<ext>` and insert unlimited employee_documents rows (no cap, no rate limit, rows accumulate per upload at line 202-205), poisoning what HR later verifies via signed URLs.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In upload_document, reject when the linked employee's status is not in ('applicant','pending_review') and when the submission is older than a short window (e.g. 48h); cap documents per reference; drop x-upsert (or store under a server-generated random object name per upload); add per-IP rate limiting. Consider invalidating GF-* refs for uploads entirely since those applicants were imported, not PWA-registered.

confirmed.title: Preparer can activate employees and change bank accounts, bypassing HR blocker/verified-bank gates, with zero audit
confirmed.evidence: main.py employee_save (123-162): `for f in ("bank_name", "bank_account", "email", "phone", "nric", ...): setattr(emp, f, ...)` and `for f in (..., "active", ...): setattr(emp, f, bool(body.get(f)))` — a `preparer` can set an arbitrary bank_account and `active=True` in one call; employee_toggle (165-173) flips `emp.active = not emp.active`. Neither path checks open blocker flags or a verified bank account (hr.py approve, lines 186-196, enforces both), neither raises an `unverified_bank_account` flag on bank change, and neither writes to audit_log (the `_audit` helper exists only in hr.py). This directly enables the §1 violation 'a payment to an unverified bank account' — silently, by the lowest-privileged role.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In employee_save/employee_toggle: forbid setting active=True unless the hr.approve gates pass (or delegate activation exclusively to POST /api/hr/employees/{id}/approve); on any bank_name/bank_account/nric change, mark the bank unverified and insert an `unverified_bank_account` blocker flag; write audit_log rows (actor, changed fields) for every employee mutation in main.py, mirroring hr.py's _audit.

confirmed.title: No audit trail for payroll-run lifecycle; runs are hard-deletable and admins can self-approve their own runs
confirmed.evidence: None of run_create/run_save/run_submit/run_approve/run_reject/run_delete writes to audit_log (grep: `_audit` is used only in hr.py). run_delete (main.py:357-365) does `db.delete(run); db.commit()` on any draft/pending/rejected run — the run and all payslips vanish with no record of who deleted what (cascade `all, delete-orphan` in models.py:168-169). run_approve (332-342) never compares `user.username` to `run.prepared_by`, so an admin (can_prepare and can_approve, models.py:69-74) can create, edit, submit and approve the same run alone. §1 requires 'an auditable trail' for pay runs; a wrong or fraudulent run can currently be created, approved, exported and then deleted without trace.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Insert audit_log rows for every run state transition and for slip edits (actor, run id, action, before/after status); replace hard delete with a soft-deleted/cancelled status (or at minimum audit-log the deletion with totals snapshot); reject approval when `run.prepared_by == user.username` unless a second approver exists (log a DECISION if the single-admin business reality requires allowing it).

confirmed.title: Session cookie not hardened: no Secure flag, no server-side invalidation, no rotation on login
confirmed.evidence: main.py:29 `app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=SECRET_KEY, max_age=60 * 60 * 12)` uses Starlette defaults: `https_only=False` (cookie sent over plain HTTP — the stack serves plain HTTP on :8077 per docker-compose.yml:33 and nginx.conf:2) and same_site defaults to 'lax'. Sessions are stateless signed cookies: logout (main.py:83-85 `request.session.clear()`) only clears the browser copy — a stolen/copied cookie remains valid for the full 12h with no server-side revocation, and login (line 78) does not rotate any session identifier.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Terminate TLS and set `https_only=True, same_site="strict"` on SessionMiddleware; add a server-side session token (e.g. random session id stored on the User row or a sessions table) checked in current_user so logout and password change actually invalidate sessions; issue a fresh session on login.

confirmed.title: Hardcoded real Google Sheet ID of a link-shared spreadsheet containing live applicant PII
confirmed.evidence: hr.py:308-309 `GOOGLE_SHEET_ID = __import__("os").environ.get("GOOGLE_SHEET_ID", "1uQxJ4Pa6YIc6bIz01WB5bBUU78V6nvtSIIU5Jv5oE_A")` and line 324 builds `https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/{GOOGLE_SHEET_ID}/export?format=xlsx`. The error message at line 329 ("check link sharing is on") confirms the sheet is meant to be link-shared, i.e. readable by anyone with the URL. Anyone with read access to this repo (or the Docker image, which contains app/) can download the entire live registration sheet — names, NRIC, bank accounts, phones — without touching the app at all. This is a new leak channel beyond the already-flagged tracked xlsx files.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Remove the hardcoded ID (default to empty and 404/501 when unset); move access to a service-account-authenticated Sheets API or turn off link sharing and proxy through the backend; rotate/retire the exposed sheet (treat the current ID as compromised and re-share to specific accounts only).

confirmed.title: Real employee PII baked into the backend Docker image and hardcoded in seed.py source
confirmed.evidence: backend/Dockerfile:9 `COPY seed.py import_legacy_form.py employee-registration-form.xlsx ./` bakes the real legacy registration workbook (NRIC, bank accounts, phones) into every built image layer — anyone with pull access to the image/registry gets the PII, independent of the git-tracked-files issue already flagged. Additionally seed.py:29-36 hardcodes 12 real employee full names in source (`ACTIVE_ROSTER = ["cheong fong cheng", "tan kui thean", ...]`, `EPF_ROSTER = [...]`).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Stop COPYing the xlsx into the image; mount it at runtime (compose volume) or fetch from a secured location only during an explicit one-off import job. Replace the hardcoded name rosters with configuration loaded from the database or an untracked env/config file; scrub existing image layers/registries that contain the workbook.

confirmed.title: seed.py force-resets every employee's active flag from a hardcoded roster on every container restart, overriding HR lifecycle decisions
confirmed.evidence: backend/Dockerfile:12 runs seed.py on every start; seed.py main() calls `configure_roster(db)` even when employees already exist (line 115-116: `print(f"Employees already present..."); configure_roster(db)`), and configure_roster (lines 60-66) does `emp.active = key in active; emp.inactive_reason = None if emp.active else "resigned"; emp.epf_enabled = key in epf` for EVERY employee. Any employee HR activated through the gated approve flow who is not in the 12-name hardcoded list is silently deactivated (unpaid) on the next restart, and anyone on the list is force-reactivated even if HR terminated them — an unauthorized, unaudited mass state change to the exact field that gates who gets paid (§6.3).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Make configure_roster run only on first import (inside the `count == 0` branch) or behind an explicit `--apply-roster` flag, never on routine startup; long term delete the hardcoded roster entirely and drive `active`/`epf_enabled` solely from the HR lifecycle endpoints, with audit_log entries for any bulk change.

confirmed.title: Upload validation trusts client-declared Content-Type only — no magic-byte verification
confirmed.evidence: registration.py:185-186 `if (file.content_type or "") not in ALLOWED_MIME: raise HTTPException(422, ...)` and lines 195-196 pick the stored extension from the same client header. The bytes are never inspected, so any payload (HTML/JS polyglot, executable, oversized decompression-bomb PDF) can be stored as `image/jpeg` in the employee-docs bucket and is later served to HR reviewers' browsers via storage.signed_url (hr.py:114) with the attacker-chosen content type.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Validate magic bytes server-side (e.g. `filetype`/Pillow verify for images, `%PDF-` header for PDFs) and reject mismatches; re-encode images where feasible; ensure Supabase serves the bucket objects with `Content-Disposition: attachment` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

confirmed.title: No security headers on the UI/nginx layer
confirmed.evidence: ui/nginx.conf (entire file, lines 1-31) sets no `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, no `X-Frame-Options`/`frame-ancestors` CSP (clickjacking of the approve/verify buttons), no `Referrer-Policy`, no HSTS, and no CSP for the SPA that renders PII. The FastAPI app adds no security-header middleware either.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add to the server block: `add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff always; add_header X-Frame-Options DENY always; add_header Referrer-Policy no-referrer always;` plus a baseline CSP (`default-src 'self'`) and HSTS once TLS is in place. Note nginx `add_header` inheritance: headers must be repeated in locations that declare their own add_header (e.g. /sw.js).

confirmed.title: Public registration endpoint has no rate limiting/anti-automation and a racy emp_code generator
confirmed.evidence: registration.py:62 `@router.post("")` is anonymous by design but has no rate limit, CAPTCHA, or per-IP quota — a script can create unbounded employees/application_submissions/hr_review_flags rows, burying the real HR queue (availability of the review workflow). emp_code assignment at lines 117-118 uses `select 'ONNI' || lpad((coalesce(max(substring(emp_code from '\d+')::int),0)+1)...` — a non-atomic read-then-insert that collides under concurrent submissions against the unique emp_code index, turning legitimate concurrent registrations into 500s.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add per-IP rate limiting (nginx `limit_req` on /api/register or slowapi in FastAPI) and a lightweight abuse control (honeypot field or CAPTCHA). Generate emp_code from a Postgres sequence (or retry-on-conflict loop) instead of max()+1.

confirmed.title: PII masking helper exists but is never applied — full NRIC/bank numbers returned everywhere, including raw submission payloads
confirmed.evidence: hr.py:49-52 defines `_mask(value, keep=4)` but it has zero call sites: detail() returns `"nric": emp.nric` (line 101), `"bank_account": emp.bank_account` (line 111), full `bank_accounts.account_no` rows (lines 83-85), and the verbatim registration `payload` JSON (lines 93-96, 119) which duplicates identity and bank numbers. serializers.employee_dict (serializers.py:44-60) likewise returns full nric/bank_account/salary to every authenticated role via GET /api/employees (main.py:97, require_user). Screens that only need to confirm 'last 4 digits' still receive the full RESTRICTED values, widening exposure in browser memory, devtools, and any future logging.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Apply `_mask` to nric/account_no in list/queue responses and in the submissions payload echo, returning full values only on the single HR detail view that needs them (or behind an explicit `?reveal=1` that is audit-logged); trim employee_dict for the general list endpoint to exclude nric/bank_account.

confirmed.title: Every container boot re-runs seed.py against the default (prod Supabase) DB, resetting passwords and rewriting the employee roster
confirmed.evidence: backend/Dockerfile:12: `CMD ["sh", "-c", "python seed.py && uvicorn app.main:app ..."]` — seed runs on EVERY start, in every environment. docker-compose.yml:21 defaults DATABASE_URL to prod Supabase via .env (run.md: "By default the backend connects to Supabase using DATABASE_URL in .env"). seed.py:75-87 `seed_users` overwrites existing users' `password_hash` with config.py defaults (preparer123/approver123/admin123, config.py:20-30); seed.py:113 and :116 call `configure_roster(db)` in BOTH branches (even when employees already exist), which sets `emp.active`, `emp.inactive_reason`, `emp.epf_enabled` for ALL employees from a hardcoded name list (seed.py:29-36) and forces `s.ft_default_epf = False; s.pt_default_epf = False`. A routine `make up` therefore mutates production master data that gates who gets paid and whose EPF is computed (§1 core guarantee, §6.3), and resets prod credentials to publicly documented demo passwords (printed by Makefile:8).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Remove seeding from the image CMD (`CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", ...]`). Move seeding to an explicit one-shot compose service or `make seed` gated to the dev profile / `APP_ENV=development`. In seed.py: never overwrite an existing user's password_hash; drop `configure_roster` from the boot path entirely (roster changes belong in the HR UI or a deliberate script run with confirmation).

confirmed.title: Default `docker compose up` targets prod Supabase; db is behind an opt-in profile and the contract's dev/test/prod profiles do not exist
confirmed.evidence: docker-compose.yml:4: `profiles: ["local-db"]        # only started with: docker compose --profile local-db up` and :20-21: `# From .env — points at Supabase; falls back to the local db service.` The skill contract requires profiles `dev`, `test`, `prod` with dev the seeded/synthetic default and prod explicit (SKILL.md Compose contract). Here the polarity is inverted: the documented everyday path (`make up`, Makefile:5; run.md Quick start) hits the production database, while the local DB is opt-in. Worse, with no `.env` present (none exists in the repo), the fallback URL `@db:5432` points at a service that never starts, so the default boot either hits prod or hangs 30s and crashes (seed.py:43-52 wait_for_db).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Restructure to contract profiles: `dev` (local db + synthetic seed + exposed ports) as the default `make up`; `test` (ephemeral db, runs suite, exits); `prod` (explicit `--profile prod`, no seeds, DATABASE_URL required with no fallback). Remove the Supabase-by-default wiring so reaching prod requires a deliberate flag plus explicit env.

confirmed.title: No migrate service: supabase/migrations are applied manually with psql, and the local-db profile never applies them — backend startup crashes on `raise_expiry_flags()`
confirmed.evidence: docker-compose.yml has services db/backend/ui only — no `migrate` service (contract: migrations "applied by a migrate service before the app starts"). README.md:54-55: "applied with psql -f" (manual). The local `db` service mounts no init scripts, so a fresh `make up-local-db` has none of supabase/migrations applied; yet backend/app/main.py:47-50 runs unguarded at startup: `if not DATABASE_URL_IS_SQLITE: db.execute(_text("select raise_expiry_flags()"))` — that function exists only in supabase/migrations/0005_status_lifecycle.sql:70, so the backend container crashes on local Postgres. Result: the only working boot path is prod Supabase, and local schema (from create_all) diverges from prod schema (RLS, views, functions from 0003-0008).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a one-shot `migrate` service (psql image) that applies supabase/migrations/*.sql in order against $DATABASE_URL, with `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy`; make backend `depends_on` migrate `service_completed_successfully`. Add `make migrate`. Until then, at minimum guard the `raise_expiry_flags()` call or fail with a clear "migrations not applied" error.

confirmed.title: App code creates tables: Base.metadata.create_all runs at every app startup and in seed.py, competing with supabase/migrations as schema source
confirmed.evidence: backend/app/database.py:31-35: `def init_db() ... Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)`, invoked from backend/app/main.py:37 (`@app.on_event("startup") ... init_db()`) and backend/seed.py:96. The infra contract names this an anti-pattern ("app code that creates tables"; "Migrations are the schema. No CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in app code"). Because the default DATABASE_URL is prod Supabase (INFRA-02), any ORM-model drift is silently materialised as new tables/columns-missing tables in production, bypassing the reviewed supabase/migrations and their RLS policies (0003_rls.sql) — new app-created tables have no RLS at all.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Delete `init_db()` from the FastAPI startup handler and from seed.py. Schema changes ship only as supabase/migrations applied by the migrate service (INFRA-03). If tests need fast schema setup, scope create_all to a pytest fixture that only accepts a test-profile DSN.

confirmed.title: `make clean` runs `docker compose down -v`, casually wiping the pgdata volume — forbidden without a human DECISION
confirmed.evidence: Makefile:21-23: `# Stop containers and wipe the local db volume\nclean:\n\tdocker compose down -v`. SKILL.md Compose contract: "`docker compose down` must not lose data; only `down -v` does, and that is never run by an agent without a human DECISION." Exposing it as an innocuously named everyday target (`clean` usually means build artifacts) invites an agent or human to destroy the only copy of local payroll data (7-year LHDN retention, §8) with one command.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Remove the `-v` from `clean` (or delete the target). If a volume-wipe target must exist, name it `nuke-local-db`, require an explicit confirmation variable (e.g. `CONFIRM=yes`), and document that running it requires a logged DECISION.

confirmed.title: Makefile lacks the contract targets: no `test`, `migrate`, `psql`, `backup`, `restore`; `up` lacks `--wait`; no backup story for a PROD-critical payroll DB
confirmed.evidence: Makefile:1: `.PHONY: up up-local-db down clean logs` — that is the complete target list. SKILL.md Agent procedure step 1 mandates `Makefile (up, down, test, migrate, psql, backup, restore)`; "`make up` → `docker compose --profile dev up -d --wait`. `make test` runs the test profile. Both are the pre-checks the judge runs." Persistence rule 4: "Backups exist before prod. Nightly pg_dump ... restore rehearsed." None exist; the only "backups" are ad-hoc dumps committed inside the repo (backups/pre-migration-20260802.sql), which is a location on/inside the host and also leaks prod data into git.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `make test` (test profile: ephemeral db + migrations + pytest), `make migrate` (runs the migrate service), `make psql` (docker compose exec db psql), `make backup`/`make restore` (pg_dump/pg_restore round-trip, target path outside the repo). Change `up` to `docker compose --profile dev up -d --build --wait`. Remove the committed dump files from the repo.

confirmed.title: .env.example is absent although .env is required for the app to boot at all
confirmed.evidence: No `.env.example` exists anywhere in the repo (root listing has no env file at all). Yet run.md:70-71: "Supabase connection details (DATABASE_URL, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY) live in .env at the repo root", and docker-compose.yml:21-26 consumes DATABASE_URL, PAYROLL_SECRET, PAYROLL_COMPANY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY. Contract: "Config: .env (gitignored) + .env.example (committed, every key documented)"; user CLAUDE.md PART 2 also mandates a documented .env.example. A fresh checkout cannot boot: without .env, backend falls back to `@db:5432` (never started by default) and dies after wait_for_db retries.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Commit `.env.example` documenting every key with safe placeholder values: DATABASE_URL, PAYROLL_SECRET, PAYROLL_COMPANY, SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY, and the seed-user override vars (PREPARER_USER/PASS, APPROVER_USER/PASS, ADMIN_USER/PASS from backend/app/config.py:20-30). Reference it from run.md setup steps.

confirmed.title: Seeds are real production data, not synthetic: real-employee xlsx baked into the Docker image and real names hardcoded in seed.py; .gitignore does not exclude the PII files
confirmed.evidence: seed.py:29-36 hardcodes real employee names: `ACTIVE_ROSTER = ["cheong fong cheng", "tan kui thean", ...]` / `EPF_ROSTER = [...]`. backend/Dockerfile:9: `COPY seed.py import_legacy_form.py employee-registration-form.xlsx ./` bakes the real registration workbook (NRIC, bank accounts, phones — §7 RESTRICTED) into every built image, from which it can be extracted by anyone with image access. Contract persistence rule 6: "Seeds are synthetic. dev seeds come from scripts/seed_*; never a production dump." Git additionally tracks emp_payroll_2605/2606.xlsx, `employee-registration-form (1).xlsx`, backend/employee-registration-form.xlsx, 2607/*.xlsx, backups/pre-migration-20260802.sql, webapp/payroll.db (the §7 known-open violation), and .gitignore:144-145 leaves the xlsx rule commented out: `# Excel files (optional...)\n# *.xlsx`.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Create `scripts/seed_dev.py` generating synthetic employees (fake NRIC/bank/names) for the dev profile; delete the xlsx COPY from backend/Dockerfile and drive real imports only via an explicit, documented operator command with the file mounted at runtime. Uncomment/add `*.xlsx`, `*.xls`, `*.db`, `backups/` to .gitignore and purge the tracked PII files from git history (git filter-repo), per the open SECURITY-FLAG.

confirmed.title: backend and ui services have no healthcheck, no restart policy, and no service_healthy dependencies; /api/health checks nothing
confirmed.evidence: docker-compose.yml:17-35: only `db` has a healthcheck; `backend` and `ui` have none, no service has `restart: unless-stopped`, and `ui` uses bare `depends_on: - backend` (no `condition: service_healthy` — impossible anyway since backend defines no healthcheck). Contract: "Every service has healthcheck, restart: unless-stopped, and depends_on with condition: service_healthy." The app relies on seed.py's wait_for_db loop instead of orchestrated ordering. backend/app/main.py:65-67 `@app.get("/api/health") ... return {"ok": True}` — it never touches the DB and omits status/version/timestamp required by the API conventions (user CLAUDE.md PART 3), so it would report healthy while the database is down.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add healthchecks: backend `curl -f http://localhost:8000/api/health`, ui `wget -qO- http://localhost/`. Add `restart: unless-stopped` to all services; `depends_on: {backend: {condition: service_healthy}}` for ui and `{db: {condition: service_healthy}}`/migrate for backend. Extend the health handler to execute `SELECT 1` and return `{status, version, timestamp}`.

confirmed.title: Both images run as root, backend image is single-stage, and no image is pinned by digest
confirmed.evidence: backend/Dockerfile has no `USER` directive (whole file, lines 1-12) — uvicorn runs as root with §7 payroll data in reach; it is also single-stage. ui/Dockerfile:10 `FROM nginx:1.27-alpine` likewise has no USER (nginx master runs as root). Images are tag-pinned only: `python:3.12-slim`, `node:20-alpine`, `nginx:1.27-alpine`, `postgres:16-alpine` (docker-compose.yml:3) — contract: "Images pinned by tag *and* digest for prod; the app image built from a multi-stage Dockerfile running as a non-root user."
confirmed.proposed_fix: backend: multi-stage build (builder installs wheels; runtime stage `adduser --system app` + `USER app`). ui: switch to `nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.27-alpine` (listen 8080). Pin all FROM lines and the compose db image with `@sha256:` digests for the prod profile.

confirmed.title: Silent SQLite fallback in config.py for a payroll API — data would land in an untracked local file / container layer
confirmed.evidence: backend/app/config.py:12-14: `DATABASE_URL = os.environ.get("DATABASE_URL", f"sqlite:///{BASE_DIR / 'payroll.db'}")`. Contract: "SQLite is acceptable only for a CLI-only surface, and only by DECISION"; anti-pattern list includes "state in a container's writable layer". If the env var is ever missing (host run, typo in .env key), the API silently starts against a file DB — payroll runs, approvals, and the audit trail get written somewhere that is not backed up and vanishes on image rebuild, breaking §1's auditable-trail guarantee. It also forces sqlite branching through the codebase (main.py:19 `DATABASE_URL_IS_SQLITE`, database.py:12).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Fail fast: raise at import/startup if DATABASE_URL is unset, unless an explicit opt-in like `APP_ENV=dev-sqlite` is set (and log a loud warning). Log the decision per the SQLite exception rule if the dev fallback is kept at all; remove the sqlite special-casing once dropped.

confirmed.title: Default secrets shipped in compose and config: forgeable session key and hardcoded DB password
confirmed.evidence: docker-compose.yml:22: `PAYROLL_SECRET: ${PAYROLL_SECRET:-change-me-in-production}` and :8 `POSTGRES_PASSWORD: payroll` hardcoded; backend/app/config.py:16: `SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("PAYROLL_SECRET", "onni-payroll-dev-secret-change-me")`. Contract: "secrets never in compose.yaml"; security gate: "secrets via .env/vault only". SECRET_KEY signs the session cookie (main.py:29 SessionMiddleware) — a deployment that forgets to set PAYROLL_SECRET runs with a public, guessable key, letting anyone forge an admin session on a system holding §7 RESTRICTED data. Demo user passwords also default in config.py:20-30 and are printed by `make up` (Makefile:8) while pointed at prod.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Remove the secret defaults: require PAYROLL_SECRET from the environment and refuse to start (outside the dev profile) when it is unset or equals a known default. Move POSTGRES_PASSWORD to .env. Gate seed-user creation to the dev profile so demo credentials can never exist in a prod DB.

confirmed.title: ui image build ignores the committed package-lock.json (`npm install` on package.json only) — unreproducible dependency tree
confirmed.evidence: ui/Dockerfile:3-4: `COPY package.json ./` then `RUN npm install` — ui/package-lock.json exists in the repo but is never copied, so every image build re-resolves semver ranges and can pull different (potentially compromised) versions than were reviewed, undermining the pinning intent of the contract's image/dependency rules.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Change to `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` and `RUN npm ci` for deterministic, lockfile-exact builds.

confirmed.title: Payroll run path pays from the boolean `active` flag and unverified employees.bank_account, bypassing the entire verification/blocker model
confirmed.evidence: payroll.py sync_new_employees/available_employees select payees with only `select(Employee).where(Employee.active.is_(True))` (lines 166, 182) — no check of status='active', open blocker flags, or a verified bank account. `_new_payslip` snapshots `bank_name=emp.bank_name, bank_account=emp.bank_account` (lines 66-67) from the legacy employees columns, not the `bank_accounts` table where the `verified` workflow lives. Meanwhile main.py lets any preparer flip the flag with no lifecycle check: `emp.active = not emp.active` (main.py:171), set it on create via `setattr(emp, f, bool(body.get(f)))` for "active" (main.py:148-150), and silently edit `bank_account`/`nric` (main.py:144-145) with no verification reset. INSERTs also bypass the DB guard entirely because trg_employees_status is `before update of status` only (0005:52-54) — seed.py/importer.py create active=True rows still in status 'applicant'. Domain R2 (blocked/unverified employees excluded from payroll) is enforced only in payroll_master_view, which the run builder never uses. Violates §1 directly: "a payment to an unverified bank account violates the guarantee".
confirmed.proposed_fix: Make payroll eligibility derive from the master model: in sync_new_employees/available_employees require status='active', no open blocker flags, and an existing verified bank account (reuse the payroll_master_view predicate); snapshot bank details from the latest verified bank_accounts row, refusing to add an employee without one. Remove `active` from the employee_save writable set and delete /api/employees/{id}/toggle (or make it call the HR lifecycle endpoints); add an INSERT trigger (or CHECK) keeping `active = (status='active')`.

confirmed.title: Session-scoped `set onni.bypass_lifecycle='1'` leaks into the connection pool, disabling status-transition enforcement for all later requests
confirmed.evidence: import_worksheet runs `db.execute(text("set onni.bypass_lifecycle = '1'"))` (line 251) — plain SET, not SET LOCAL — and is called from the live endpoint POST /api/hr/sync-google-sheet with the request session (hr.py:336). The GUC is never RESET; SQLAlchemy's pool reset-on-return (rollback) does not clear session GUCs, so after one sheet sync the pooled connection permanently satisfies `current_setting('onni.bypass_lifecycle', true) = '1'` in check_status_transition (0005:26), and every subsequent request served on that connection skips transition validation and the resigned/terminated required-date checks. Lifecycle enforcement (lifecycle.md R1, §6.3 activation gate) is silently off for a random subset of traffic.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Use a transaction-scoped setting: `SELECT set_config('onni.bypass_lifecycle','1', true)` (or `SET LOCAL`) inside the import transaction, and/or `RESET onni.bypass_lifecycle` in a finally block. Better: run the sheet sync on a dedicated short-lived connection, not the pooled request session.

confirmed.title: HR approve accepts status 'applicant' but the DB trigger forbids applicant→active — activation 500s for every payroll-UI-created or seeded employee
confirmed.evidence: hr.py approve: `if emp.status not in ("applicant", "pending_review"): raise ...` (line 183) then inserts a status-history row 'active'; apply_status_history updates employees.status, firing check_status_transition where the allowed set from 'applicant' is only `('pending_review','rejected')` (0005:31). So approving an applicant raises `invalid status transition applicant -> active` → unhandled 500. Every employee created by POST /api/employees (main.py never sets status → model default 'applicant', models.py:117) or by seed.py/importer.py sits in 'applicant' and appears in the HR queue (hr.py:64 queries both statuses) but cannot be activated — except when the DL-02 GUC leak happens to be active, making behavior nondeterministic.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Pick one contract and enforce it both places: either allow applicant→active in check_status_transition, or have the approve endpoint first insert a 'pending_review' history row for applicants before the 'active' row (and update the trigger comment/lifecycle.md R1 accordingly). Add a test that approves an 'applicant'-status employee against Postgres.

confirmed.title: audit_log is written only by the HR router — zero audit on payroll §6 actions (run approve/reject, payslip edits, statutory settings, bank/salary edits, exports)
confirmed.evidence: grep shows all `_audit(...)` call sites live in hr.py only. main.py mutations write nothing to audit_log: run_approve (line 332-342), run_reject, run_submit, run_delete, run_save (payslip money edits), settings_save (EPF/SOCSO/EIS/PCB rates — line 444-462), employee_save (bank_account/NRIC/salary — line 123-162), employee_toggle (line 165). payroll_export.py master/movements CSV downloads (the feed for actual bank payments, §6.4) are also unaudited. §1 requires "an auditable trail"; today a preparer can change a bank account and an approver can approve a run with no audit_log row.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Move `_audit` into a shared module (e.g. app/audit.py) and call it from every §6 mutation: employee create/edit/toggle (with changed_fields), run submit/approve/reject/delete, run_save (slip ids changed), settings_save (fields changed), and payroll-export downloads (action='export', entity='payroll_master', entity_id='YYYY-MM'). Keep values out — field names and ids only, as _audit already does.

confirmed.title: Re-running the sheet sync deletes ALL satellite rows for matched employees — including HR-verified bank accounts, PWA-uploaded documents, and the append-only status history
confirmed.evidence: For every non-settled employee the import wipes indiscriminately: `for tbl in ("bank_accounts", "emergency_contacts", "employee_documents"): db.execute(text(f"delete from {tbl} where employee_id = :eid"))` (lines 355-356) — unlike flags, which are filtered `raised_by = 'import'` (line 357). It then also runs `delete from employee_status_history where employee_id = :eid` (line 361). A bank account HR verified while the employee was still pending_review (verification is a precondition of approval, so it normally happens in this status) is destroyed and re-inserted verified=false; PWA-uploaded document rows (storage_path references) are dropped; and the append-only history mandated by lifecycle.md R1/R5 ("History append-only") is erased. POST /api/hr/sync-google-sheet makes this a routine button, not a one-shot.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a source/raised_by discriminator to bank_accounts, emergency_contacts and employee_documents (e.g. `source text default 'import'`) and delete only `source='import'` rows, mirroring the flags handling; never delete employee_status_history — insert a new row only when target_status differs from the current latest. Preserve `verified=true` bank rows unconditionally.

confirmed.title: Seed importer silently 'fixes' float-corrupted NRIC/bank cells, raises no flags, and activates employees — violating the zero-silent-fixes rule
confirmed.evidence: importer.py `_clean`: `if isinstance(value, float) and value.is_integer(): return str(int(value))` (lines 95-96) is applied to nric and bank_account cells (lines 147-148) — a spreadsheet cell that went numeric (lost leading zero, float-precision-mangled 15-16 digit account) is stored as-is with no hr_review_flags row, directly contradicting lifecycle.md R6 ("every recovery/guess raises a flag — zero silent fixes") and H2 ("15–16-digit values at float precision are always blocker-flagged"). Each row is then created `active=True` (line 154) with no HR review, and via DL-01 those bank digits flow onto payslips. import_employees is also non-idempotent: it appends every row on each call (only seed.py's count==0 check guards it), and emp_code `f"ONNI{seq:04d}"` seeded from `count(*)` (line 125) collides with existing codes after any deletion.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Route seeding through import_legacy_form.import_worksheet (which has the recovery+flag logic and GF-<row> idempotency) and delete importer.py's duplicate path; at minimum, make _clean flag float-sourced nric/bank values as blockers, create employees inactive/pending_review, and key rows on reg_ref for idempotent re-runs.

confirmed.title: Two schema sources: startup create_all vs SQL migrations — fresh-Postgres boot fails on missing enum types, SQLite fallback lacks all 9 master tables
confirmed.evidence: main.py startup calls init_db() (main.py:37) → `Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)` (database.py:35) unconditionally, including against prod Postgres. Employee.status/identity_type use `postgresql.ENUM(..., create_type=False)` (models.py:113-123), so on a fresh Postgres where migrations haven't run, CREATE TABLE employees references types employment_status/identity_type that don't exist and startup crashes — there is no migrate step in compose (§10 gap). Conversely on the SQLite dev fallback create_all builds only the 5 model tables; hr_review_flags, bank_accounts, application_submissions, audit_log etc. exist solely in supabase/migrations, so every /api/hr, /api/register and /api/payroll-export endpoint 500s (their raw SQL is also Postgres-only: `::text`, `on conflict`, `now()`).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Declare migrations the single schema source for Postgres: run create_all only when DATABASE_URL_IS_SQLITE, and add a migrate step (psql loop over supabase/migrations, or a compose `migrate` service) that runs before the API starts. Either give the master tables SQLAlchemy models + SQLite-compatible SQL, or explicitly disable the hr/registration/export routers on SQLite instead of letting them 500.

confirmed.title: pay_profiles (integer sen, the declared master pay record) is write-only — payroll and the master CSV read salary from legacy employees.basic_salary instead
confirmed.evidence: payroll_master_view exposes `(e.basic_salary * 100)::integer as basic_salary_sen, (e.hourly_rate * 100)::integer as hourly_rate_sen` (0004:19-20) — legacy RM columns — while pay_profiles.basic_salary_sen written at approval (hr.py:225-234) is only consulted for ot_eligible/epf_no. After activation there is no endpoint that updates pay_profiles (approve is one-shot; effective_to is never closed), but main.py employee_save freely rewrites employees.basic_salary (main.py:141) with no audit and run_save even back-fills it from a payslip (main.py:297-298). Result: two divergent salary records, with the HR-approved sen value inert and the unaudited RM value feeding both the payroll run and the bank-payment CSV.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Pick employees.basic_salary/hourly_rate as the single operational pay source and drop the pay_profiles columns from the flow (or vice versa): if pay_profiles stays authoritative, change the view to `coalesce(pp.basic_salary_sen, (e.basic_salary*100)::integer)`, add an HR pay-change endpoint that closes the old row (effective_to) and inserts a new one with an audit_log entry, and make employee_save reject direct salary edits for status='active' employees.

confirmed.title: Money-representation rule drift: RM NUMERIC(12,2) storage (float on SQLite) and float round-trips in the sen conversion on the approval path
confirmed.evidence: PROJECT_PROFILE §3 / runs-and-exports R4: "Money is integer sen in the DB … never floats for storage or math." models.py stores all payslip/employee/settings money as `MONEY = Numeric(12, 2)` RM (models.py:15) — on the sanctioned SQLite dev fallback SQLAlchemy persists Numeric as REAL (float storage), and migrate_sqlite.py then copies those floats into Postgres. hr.py approve converts money through float: `"b": int(round(float(basic or emp.basic_salary or 0) * 100)) or None` (hr.py:230-231) — a float in a §6 money path; also `or None` turns a legitimate 0 into NULL, tripping the pay_profiles CHECK for a zero-salary monthly profile.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Convert via Decimal on the approval path: `int((Decimal(str(basic)) * 100).quantize(Decimal('1')))`, and treat 0 explicitly instead of `or None`. Document a DECISION that the payslip tables intentionally stay NUMERIC(12,2) RM (contradicting §3) or plan the sen migration; forbid float in any sen conversion via a lint/test.

confirmed.title: raise_expiry_flags never escalates an expired typhoid cert to blocker while the earlier 'typhoid_expiring' warning is still open
confirmed.evidence: The dedup predicate for the typhoid insert excludes both flag types: `and not exists (... f.flag_type in ('typhoid_expiring','typhoid_expired') and (f.details->>'doc_id')::bigint = d.id)` (0005:85-88). Sequence: 25 days before expiry a 'typhoid_expiring' warning is raised; when the cert actually expires, the open warning suppresses the 'typhoid_expired' blocker insert, so the employee is never blocked from payroll_master_view and keeps handling food with an expired KKM-mandatory cert until HR happens to resolve the warning.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Split the dedup per resulting flag_type (`f.flag_type = case when d.expiry_date < current_date then 'typhoid_expired' else 'typhoid_expiring' end`), and auto-resolve the open 'typhoid_expiring' warning when inserting the 'typhoid_expired' blocker for the same doc_id.

confirmed.title: payroll_movements_view classifies every leaver as 'hire_and_leave' — movement labels ignore the reporting period
confirmed.evidence: `case when e.hire_date is not null and e.last_working_day is not null then 'hire_and_leave' when e.last_working_day is not null then 'leaver' else 'new_hire' end` (0004:66-70). Activation always sets hire_date (hr.py:217), so any employee resigning later has both dates and is exported as 'hire_and_leave' in the movements CSV (payroll_export.py:56-66) even when hired years earlier; 'leaver' is unreachable for normally-activated staff. The movements CSV drives the clerk's final-pay handling (runs-and-exports R3/H1), so the mislabel invites wrong month-boundary treatment.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Compute movement in the export query where the period is known, e.g. new_hire = hire_date within [month), leaver = last_working_day within [month), hire_and_leave = both within the same month; keep the view exposing raw dates only (drop its movement column) so the label can't be computed without a period.

confirmed.title: Hardcoded live Google Sheet ID (source of real NRIC/bank data) committed as the in-code default
confirmed.evidence: `GOOGLE_SHEET_ID = __import__("os").environ.get("GOOGLE_SHEET_ID", "1uQxJ4Pa6YIc6bIz01WB5bBUU78V6nvtSIIU5Jv5oE_A")` (hr.py:308-309) with the fetch requiring link-sharing to be on (hr.py:324-329). ACTIVE_ROSTER real employee names are likewise hardcoded (import_legacy_form.py:38-43, seed.py:29-34).

Move the active roster out of code into data (a DB column or an ops-provided file) so real names stop shipping in the repo.

confirmed.title: Concurrent registrations race on MAX()-based emp_code generation — duplicate ONNI codes crash the public submit endpoint
confirmed.evidence: `select 'ONNI' || lpad((coalesce(max(substring(emp_code from '\d+')::int),0)+1)::text, 4, '0') from employees` (registration.py:117-118, duplicated in import_legacy_form.py:312-313). Two concurrent anonymous submissions read the same max and both insert the same emp_code; ix_employees_emp_code is unique, so the second applicant gets an unhandled IntegrityError 500 and their submission (including uploaded-doc reference) is lost. Traffic is low but this is the public PWA path.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Allocate codes from a Postgres sequence (`create sequence onni_emp_code_seq`; `'ONNI' || lpad(nextval(...)::text, 4, '0')`), or retry on unique violation. Share one helper between registration.py and import_legacy_form.py.

confirmed.title: audit_log has no indexes and no tamper protection; duplicate-detection columns unindexed
confirmed.evidence: audit_log (0002:151-159) is created with only its PK — no index on (entity, entity_id) or created_at, so per-employee audit lookups are seq scans; nothing prevents UPDATE/DELETE on it (RLS locks out anon keys, but the backend/owner connection can rewrite history — the trail §1 relies on is not append-only at the DB level). The registration duplicate check filters on employees.nric / lower(email) / phone (registration.py:108-112) with no supporting indexes. Impact is small at ~200 employees, hence low.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `create index on audit_log (entity, entity_id)` and `(created_at)`; enforce append-only with `create rule` / trigger raising on UPDATE/DELETE (or revoke UPDATE/DELETE from the app role). Add indexes on employees (nric), (lower(email)), (phone) for the dup check.

confirmed.title: Naive local timestamps and TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE on payroll approval fields, against the §8 timestamptz rule
confirmed.evidence: run_submit/run_approve stamp `dt.datetime.now()` (main.py:327, 340) — naive container-local time — into columns defined `TIMESTAMP WITHOUT TIME ZONE` (0001:43-45); models.py likewise uses `DateTime` without timezone for users/employees/payroll_runs created_at (e.g. models.py:66, 139, 164). PROJECT_PROFILE §8 mandates `timestamptz` with Asia/Kuala_Lumpur; approval times on the irreversible §6.2 path are ambiguous (UTC container vs KL) and will mislead month-end-window audits by 8 hours.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Use `dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc)` in the app, change the model columns to `DateTime(timezone=True)`, and add a migration altering payroll_runs/users/employees timestamp columns to timestamptz (values interpreted as UTC).

confirmed.title: migrate_sqlite.py wipe-and-replace fails or orphans master data on any target that has satellite rows
confirmed.evidence: The script deletes payslips→runs→employees→users→settings (`for model in reversed(MODELS): dst.execute(delete(model))`, lines 30-31) but knows nothing of the 9 master tables: any bank_accounts/hr_review_flags/application_submissions rows referencing employees make `delete(employees)` fail with an FK violation, so the tool is unusable once master data exists — and if it ever succeeded (empty satellites) it would still bulk-insert employees with arbitrary status values, bypassing the lifecycle trigger (insert-path gap, see DL-01). It also wipes payroll history, in tension with §8's 7-year retention if pointed at a live target.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Guard the script: refuse to run if the target has rows in any master-data table (or any payslips), print what would be destroyed, and require an explicit --force. Document it as bootstrap-only in the module docstring and README.

confirmed.title: Statutory engine's only regression guard (self-test) fails on current code and is never executed
confirmed.evidence: The `if __name__ == "__main__":` self-test asserts `(r.socso_employee, r.socso_employer) == (Decimal("24.75"), Decimal("86.65"))` and `r.net_salary == Decimal("4305.35")`. Note the domain doc's own W1 row (SOCSO 24.75/86.65) is also stale relative to R3 (employee 1.25%).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Move the self-test into pytest golden tests (tests/test_statutory.py) with expected figures recomputed under the current legislated rates (employee 1.25% per PERKESO Circular 2/2026), delete the __main__ block (or keep it delegating to pytest), wire `pytest` into the Makefile and CI so the guard actually runs, and update W1 in .claude/domain/payroll/statutory.md to match.

confirmed.title: SOCSO employee rate duplicated in Settings ORM default (0.005) and diverged from engine constant (0.0125) — live compute path uses the stale rate
confirmed.evidence: models.py: `socso_c1_emp: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(RATE, default=Decimal("0.005"))` while core/rates.py has `SOCSO_C1_EMP = Decimal("0.0125")`. Every live computation goes through `store.rate_config(db)` (main.py run_save/add_slip/sync call it), which builds RateConfig from the Settings row — so any Settings row created by `store.get_settings()` computes SOCSO employee share at 0.5%, not the legislated 1.25% (domain R3, effective 1 Jun 2026). No migration in supabase/migrations/ updates existing rows either (grep for socso_c1_emp only hits the 0001 column definition). The 'Fix EPF and SOCSO' commit 587d436 changed only core/rates.py, so the fix never reached the DB-driven live path — a wrong statutory figure directly violating the §1 core guarantee, caused by the same rate being defined in two unlinked places.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Make Settings defaults derive from the engine constants (e.g. `default=rates.SOCSO_C1_EMP` for every shared field) so there is one source of truth; ship a data migration/seed step updating existing settings rows (`update settings set socso_c1_emp = 0.0125 where socso_c1_emp = 0.005`); add a unit test asserting `RateConfig()` equals a RateConfig built from a freshly-defaulted Settings row.

confirmed.title: No test suite exists anywhere in the live app — every §6 high-risk path is unguarded
confirmed.evidence: `find` shows zero test_*.py, conftest.py, pytest.ini or tests/ directories outside webapp/ (which has none either). The user's global standard mandates pytest tests mirroring src with 80% coverage; the domain files define exact scenarios that must be locked down (statutory.md W1–W3, H1–H6; runs-and-exports.md H1–H3) and L1 records that EPF/SOCSO already regressed once. Required suites, none of which exist: (1) tests/core/test_kwsp.py — band_upper RM20 edges (5000.00 vs 5000.01), employer 13%→12% threshold flip, roundup_ringgit (H2); (2) tests/core/test_socso.py — W1 golden, exclusive-lower band edges RM30/50/70/100 (H3), RM6,000 ceiling, over_60 Category 2, documented H1 5-sen tie cases; (3) tests/core/test_eis.py — foreign-worker and age-60 exclusion (R4/H5); (4) tests/core/test_pcb.py — rebate edge at CI=35,000, zero-CI, pcb_override precedence (H6); (5) tests/test_statutory.py — W1–W3 goldens, include_allowance/include_ot combinations, R7 net/employer-cost identities; (6) tests/test_payroll.py — recompute + lindung deduction, run lifecycle draft→pending→approved→locked, idempotent add/sync (runs H3); (7) tests/test_rbac.py — require_preparer/approver/admin and PayrollRun.editable_by state matrix; (8) tests/test_hr_activation.py — approve blocked on open blocker flags, unverified bank, missing position/salary (activation gate); (9) tests/test_exports.py — master CSV excludes blocked employees, month-boundary joins/leavers windows (runs H1), sen→RM conversion; (10) tests/test_registration.py — NRIC/phone/bank validation, duplicate detection flag, upload size/MIME limits.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Create tests/ mirroring backend/app with the ten suites above (pytest, markers per standard, DB-backed suites against the compose Postgres with migrations applied), enforce 80% coverage via pytest-cov, and gate `make up`/CI on them. Prioritize (1)–(5) — pure functions, no DB needed — in the first pass since they guard the core guarantee directly.

confirmed.title: No pyproject.toml, lint/type/test config, dev dependencies, or CI — and ruff/mypy currently fail
confirmed.evidence: Repo root and backend/ contain no pyproject.toml, setup.py/cfg, pytest.ini, ruff/black/mypy config, and no .github/ CI; backend/requirements.txt lists only runtime deps (fastapi, sqlalchemy, …) with no pytest/ruff/black/mypy; the Makefile has only up/down/clean/logs targets. Running the mandated checks fails: `ruff check backend` → 10 errors (F401 unused imports in app/hr.py:10 `json`, app/security.py:13 `select`, app/statutory.py:16 `round5, roundup_ringgit`, import_legacy_form.py:30 `Session`; E402 in app/main.py:20-25 caused by `DATABASE_URL_IS_SQLITE` being assigned mid-import-block at main.py:19); `mypy app --ignore-missing-imports` → 11 errors in 3 files (e.g. payroll.py:34 Decimal|int arg-type, hr.py:147 Result.rowcount attr-defined).
