confirmed.title: Dead settings: default_include_allowance / default_include_ot are stored and admin-editable but never read by any code path
confirmed.evidence: Settings defines `default_include_allowance` / `default_include_ot`, main.py SETTING_KINDS exposes them for admin editing and serializers.py returns them, but grep shows no consumer: payroll.py hardcodes `include_allowance=True, include_ot=False` in _new_payslip (lines 74-75) and main.py run_save re-hardcodes `slip.include_allowance = True; slip.include_ot = False` (lines 294-295). An admin toggling these statutory-wage-composition settings (domain R1: allowance/OT attract statutory only when opted in) sees no effect — misleading dead configuration on a money path.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Either wire the settings through (_new_payslip and run_save read them from the Settings row instead of hardcoding) or delete the two columns from Settings, SETTING_KINDS, SETTINGS_FIELDS and the UI, documenting that statutory base is fixed at basic+allowance. Add a test pinning whichever behavior is chosen.

confirmed.title: Zero logging in the entire backend; startup errors swallowed by silent broad excepts; print() used in operational scripts
confirmed.evidence: grep finds no `import logging`/`getLogger` anywhere under backend/. main.py _startup wraps `storage.ensure_bucket()` in `except Exception:\n        pass` — a failed/misconfigured document bucket (RESTRICTED PDPA documents) is silently ignored with no trace. importer.py:32 uses broad `except Exception: return None` where `decimal.InvalidOperation` is the specific failure. Operational scripts (seed.py, migrate_sqlite.py, import_legacy_form.py — 14 call sites) report via print() only. The global standard mandates the logging module and specific exception types.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; in _startup catch `httpx.HTTPError` and log at warning with the failure reason; in importer._to_number catch `decimal.InvalidOperation, ValueError`; convert script print() calls to logging with a basicConfig in each __main__ entry.

confirmed.title: All mutation endpoints take untyped `body: dict = Body(...)` — no Pydantic validation on money-critical inputs, malformed input yields 500s
confirmed.evidence: Every POST/PUT in main.py, hr.py and registration.py declares `body: dict = Body(...)`. run_create does `year, month = int(body["year"]), int(body["month"])` — a missing key raises KeyError → 500 instead of 422, and month=13 is accepted, creating an unusable run (`period_label` then raises IndexError on MONTHS[13] in every subsequent /api/runs listing, breaking the runs page). run_save's slips loop does `int(s["id"])` similarly. `dict` bodies are implicit Any, violating the mandatory-type-hints standard, and no bounds exist on payroll figures (negative basic, month 0).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Define Pydantic request models (RunCreate with year: int = Field(ge=2020), month: int = Field(ge=1, le=12); SlipUpdate; EmployeeSave; ApproveBody; RegistrationBody) so FastAPI returns 422 with field detail automatically; validate ranges on all money/units fields.

confirmed.title: HR activation path converts money via float and coerces zero to NULL when writing pay_profiles sen values
confirmed.evidence: approve() writes the pay profile that feeds the payroll master CSV (which feeds actual bank payments) with `"b": int(round(float(basic or emp.basic_salary or 0) * 100)) or None` and the same pattern for hourly — float math on money violates domain R6 / PRD ground rule 6 (Decimal in engine, integer sen in DB, floats only at the serialization edge), and the trailing `or None` silently turns a legitimate 0 into NULL. It also assigns the raw JSON value directly to a Decimal column (`emp.basic_salary = basic` at line 214) with no Decimal coercion, unlike main.py which uses _dec().
confirmed.proposed_fix: Convert with Decimal end-to-end: `sen = int((D(basic or emp.basic_salary or 0) * 100).to_integral_value(ROUND_HALF_UP))`; store 0 as 0 and use an explicit `if pay_type == 'monthly'` to decide which column is NULL; coerce body values via the shared _dec/D helper before assigning to ORM Decimal columns.

confirmed.title: Statutory engine exists in three diverged copies (backend/app, webapp/app, build_payroll.py) — divergence already produced conflicting rates
confirmed.evidence: webapp/app/core/* is a near-copy of backend/app/core/* (statutory.py, eis.py, pcb.py byte-identical; socso.py/kwsp.py/rates.py diverged — webapp still has `SOCSO_C1_EMP = Decimal("0.005")`). Repo-root build_payroll.py (the tool that produced the real 2607/*.xlsx payroll workbooks) is a third implementation with `("SOCSO Cat 1 employee %", 0.005, ...)` at line 105 and EPF computed as `ROUNDUP(Gross*rate)` on the raw wage (line 407) — both contradicting the fixed backend engine (1.25% employee, EPF on RM20 band upper bound per domain R2/H2). The 587d436 fix landed in exactly one of the three copies; the other two still generate wrong statutory figures if anyone runs them, and byte-identical statutory.py invites cross-porting stale code.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Quarantine hard: delete build_payroll.py and webapp/app/core (or move both under a clearly-named legacy/ directory excluded from tooling and add a top-of-file banner 'STALE RATES — do not use'); if the Excel builder must stay runnable, refactor it to import rates/figures from backend.app.core so there is one engine; add a repo test that fails if any file outside backend/ defines SOCSO/EPF rate constants.

confirmed.title: Missing return-type annotations and docstrings across the public API surface; core calculators take untyped wage params
confirmed.evidence: Aggregated per module (standard mandates type hints and Google-style docstrings on all public functions): main.py — ~30 endpoint functions, almost none have return annotations or docstrings (e.g. `def health():`, `def login(request, body, db):`); hr.py — 13 of 15 endpoints lack both; registration.py, payroll_export.py similar; serializers.py `_num(v)` fully untyped; core modules kwsp/socso/eis/pcb declare `def contribution(wage, ...)` / `def band_upper(wage, ...)` with the money-bearing `wage` parameter untyped (implicit Any) despite Decimal-typed returns; models.py `editable_by(self, user)` user untyped.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Annotate endpoint returns (dict / Response), type `wage: Decimal | int | str` (or a Money alias) on all core calculator signatures, type `user: User` in editable_by, and add one-line Google-style docstrings to each public endpoint; enforce with ruff ANN + D rules in the new pyproject.

confirmed.title: Request-time sys.path mutation and __import__ hack with a real hardcoded Google Sheet ID fallback
confirmed.evidence: `GOOGLE_SHEET_ID = __import__("os").environ.get("GOOGLE_SHEET_ID", "1uQxJ4Pa6YIc6bIz01WB5bBUU78V6nvtSIIU5Jv5oE_A")` — a real production sheet id committed as a code default (the sheet holds applicant PII per §7), plus a gratuitous __import__ instead of the module's imports. sync_google_sheet (line 331) does `_sys.path.insert(0, ...)` on every request to import import_legacy_form — sys.path grows per call and the import layout depends on the container's file placement.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Move GOOGLE_SHEET_ID into config.py with `os.environ.get("GOOGLE_SHEET_ID", "")` (empty default; endpoint returns 503 when unset), and move import_legacy_form.py's import_worksheet into the app package (e.g. app/legacy_import.py) so it is a normal top-level import with no path mutation.

confirmed.title: Employee-code generation via select max()+1 is race-prone and 500s on collision
confirmed.evidence: `code = db.scalar(text("select 'ONNI' || lpad((coalesce(max(substring(emp_code from '\\d+')::int),0)+1)::text, 4, '0') from employees"))` — two concurrent public registrations (anonymous PWA endpoint) can read the same max and both insert the same emp_code; the unique constraint on employees.emp_code then raises IntegrityError → unhandled 500 for the applicant, and the transaction's satellite rows are lost.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Allocate from a Postgres sequence (e.g. `create sequence emp_code_seq`, code = 'ONNI' || lpad(nextval(...))) or catch IntegrityError and retry the insert with a fresh code; add a concurrency test with two parallel submissions.

confirmed.title: Module-level `assert` guards API/serializer field consistency — stripped under python -O; deprecated on_event startup hook
confirmed.evidence: `assert set(SETTING_KINDS) == set(SETTINGS_FIELDS)` is the only guard keeping the settings API and serializer in sync; running uvicorn under `python -O` removes it silently. Startup logic uses `@app.on_event("startup")` (main.py:35), deprecated since FastAPI 0.93 in favor of lifespan handlers — the pinned fastapi==0.115.6 emits DeprecationWarning and future upgrades will break it.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Replace the assert with `if set(SETTING_KINDS) != set(SETTINGS_FIELDS): raise RuntimeError(...)` (or better, a unit test), and migrate _startup to a lifespan context manager passed to FastAPI(lifespan=...).

confirmed.title: Health endpoint returns only {ok: true} — no status/version/timestamp per the API convention
confirmed.evidence: `@app.get("/api/health")\ndef health():\n    return {"ok": True}` — the user's global API convention (CLAUDE.md Part 3) requires every API to expose a health endpoint returning status, version, and timestamp; there is no version identifier anywhere in the app, so deployed-version verification during the month-end payroll window (§12) is impossible.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Return `{"status": "ok", "version": APP_VERSION, "timestamp": dt.datetime.now(dt.timezone.utc).isoformat()}` with APP_VERSION sourced from config/env (set at image build), and add a DB connectivity check (`select 1`) so the healthcheck actually reflects serviceability.

confirmed.title: PWA manifest icons do not exist — installability (PRD Phase 5 hard requirement) fails
confirmed.evidence: Manifest declares `{ src: '/icons/icon-192.png', sizes: '192x192', type: 'image/png', purpose: 'any maskable' }` and the 512 equivalent, and `includeAssets: ['style.css', 'icons/icon-192.png', 'icons/icon-512.png']` — but `ui/public/` contains only `style.css` (no `icons/` directory anywhere in the repo). Both icon URLs 404 at runtime, so Chrome's installability check and Lighthouse PWA audit fail. PRD Phase 5: "Web app manifest (name, icons incl. 192/512 maskable...), installable on Android/iOS" and acceptance criterion 5 "PWA deployed ... installable". README.md:114 already claims "installable (manifest + service worker)", which is currently false. There is also no apple-touch-icon/meta for iOS in ui/index.html.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add real 192x192 and 512x512 PNGs under ui/public/icons/. Declare separate entries for `purpose: 'any'` and `purpose: 'maskable'` (combined 'any maskable' is flagged by Lighthouse and crops badly). Add `<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="/icons/icon-192.png">` to ui/index.html for iOS. Verify with Lighthouse PWA audit before claiming installability in README.

confirmed.title: Production styling depends on the Tailwind Play CDN — third-party runtime script, no SRI, breaks offline app shell
confirmed.evidence: `<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"></script>` — the Play CDN is explicitly "not for production" (it JIT-compiles CSS in the browser on every load and logs a console warning). It is a render-blocking, un-pinned, no-SRI third-party script on a payroll app (supply-chain exposure for RESTRICTED data screens). Offline/app-shell: vite.config.js works around it with a CacheFirst runtimeCaching rule for cdn.tailwindcss.com, so the shell is unstyled on any first visit where the CDN is unreachable, and the PRD's "precache app shell" requirement is only met via a mutable third-party fetch. Also violates PROJECT_PROFILE §11 ("UI bundle default budget applies").
confirmed.proposed_fix: Install Tailwind as a build-time dependency (@tailwindcss/vite or PostCSS plugin), move the inline `tailwind.config` (brand/moss colors) into tailwind.config.js, emit a hashed CSS asset that vite-plugin-pwa precaches, and delete both the CDN <script> in index.html and the `cdn` runtimeCaching entry in vite.config.js.

confirmed.title: Offline-queued registration silently drops all uploaded documents with no retry path
confirmed.evidence: On offline submit only the JSON form is queued: `await idbSet(QUEUE_KEY, { form: payload, at: Date.now() })` — the `files` state (NRIC front/back, food-handler cert, typhoid proof, etc.) is never persisted to IndexedDB. When `flushQueue()` later succeeds (lines 86–94) it posts the form, sets `docs: 'pending'`, and never calls `uploadDocs`, so the documents are permanently lost; the success screen offers no re-upload UI. PRD Phase 5 hard requirement: "Uploads retry when back online." Consequence: submissions arrive without mandatory KKM documents, `missing_document` flags block activation, and HR must chase every spotty-connection applicant.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Persist the selected files (File/Blob store fine in IndexedDB) alongside the queued form: `idbSet(QUEUE_KEY, { form, files, at })`. In flushQueue, after obtaining the reference number, run uploadDocs with the stored blobs and report per-document status; keep failed docs queued. Also surface a re-upload screen keyed by reference number for docs that failed after an online submit.

confirmed.title: Registration queue race can double-submit, and navigator.onLine misdetection skips queueing on flaky networks
confirmed.evidence: (1) `flushQueue()` is invoked from both the mount effect (line 77) and every 'online' event (line 73) with no in-flight guard; two concurrent calls both read QUEUE_KEY before either deletes it, POSTing /api/register twice and creating duplicate applicant records (domain hazard H4 says duplicates must be flagged, so this pollutes the HR queue). (2) The queue branch is gated on `if (!navigator.onLine)` — when fetch fails while onLine is true (captive portal, DNS failure, backend down: the exact "spotty-connection" case the PRD names), the submission is NOT queued; the applicant just sees the raw error. (3) A successful flush also overwrites any new form the applicant is currently filling via `setDone(...)` (line 92).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Add a module-level in-flight flag (or delete QUEUE_KEY before posting and restore on failure) so flushQueue is single-flight. Queue on any network-level failure (err instanceof TypeError) regardless of navigator.onLine. Only setDone from flushQueue when the form is untouched, otherwise show a small banner ("your earlier registration was sent — ref GF-xxx").

confirmed.title: Demo credentials for all three roles are hardcoded into the Login page and ship in every build
confirmed.evidence: `Demo accounts — preparer/preparer123 · approver/approver123 · admin/admin123` is rendered unconditionally. actors.md marks these as "TRIAL-only; must never reach prod", and PROJECT_PROFILE §13 classifies the system PROD-critical with real data already present. Any deployment of this build advertises working admin credentials on the login screen — an outsider can approve payroll runs, edit statutory rates, and read every NRIC/bank account, directly violating the §1 core guarantee.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Gate the hint behind `import.meta.env.DEV` (or a backend-provided `demo_mode` flag from /api/auth/me), so production bundles never contain the string. Pair with the backend fix that stops seeding these accounts outside trial mode.

confirmed.title: Payroll run: unsaved cell edits are silently excluded when submitting/approving — approved run can differ from what the preparer sees
confirmed.evidence: `const submit = () => window.confirm('Save your edits first. Send for approval now?') && act(() => api.post(`/api/runs/${runId}/submit`), ...)` — Send only changes status; `setField` edits (basic, OT hours, deductions, PCB override) live purely in local state until the separate "Save & Recalculate" button posts them. A preparer who types a deduction and clicks Send submits the last-saved figures while their screen still shows the edited ones; the approver then locks a run that pays the wrong net salary (§1 violation). There is also no dirty-state indicator and no navigation/beforeunload guard, so edits are lost without warning on route change.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Track dirty state (compare slips vs detail.slips). Make Send first persist: `await api.put(`/api/runs/${runId}`, { remarks, slips })` then POST /submit (or disable Send while dirty with an explicit "unsaved changes" badge). Add a router blocker/beforeunload prompt while dirty. Same for the Dashboard approve path if edits are pending.

confirmed.title: No 401/session-expiry handling and several pages have no error or loading state — failures render a permanent blank page
confirmed.evidence: `const load = () => api.get('/api/hr/queue').then((d) => setQueue(d.queue))` has no `.catch` — a failed load is an unhandled rejection and the page stays at `if (!queue) return null` forever (blank screen, no message). Same in HRCompliance.jsx:9 (`api.get('/api/hr/compliance').then(setData)`). Globally, ui/src/api.js throws ApiError but nothing reacts to status 401: App.jsx checks /api/auth/me once at mount, so when the session cookie expires mid-shift every click just flashes an error over a dead UI — during the month-end payroll window this stalls the critical journey. Every page also uses `return null` while loading (no spinner/skeleton), and Employees.jsx renders a header-only table when a filter matches zero rows.
confirmed.proposed_fix: In api.js, on `res.status === 401` dispatch a handler that clears the user in App context (returning to <Login/> while preserving the current route for post-login redirect). Add `.catch((e) => flash(e.message, 'error'))` plus a visible error state to HRQueue and HRCompliance. Introduce shared <Loading/> and <ErrorState retry={load}/> components used by all pages instead of `return null`, and an empty-row message in Employees.

confirmed.title: money() renders legitimate zero amounts as '-' on payslips and payroll tables
confirmed.evidence: `export const money = (v) => { const n = Number(v || 0); return n ? n.toLocaleString(...) : '-' }` — 0 is falsy, so a true RM0.00 figure (EPF for a non-opted foreign worker, PCB 0, zero deduction) displays as '-' on the on-screen payslip (Payslip.jsx deduction rows) and the run table, indistinguishable from "not applicable". On a statutory pay document that ambiguity invites disputes and mis-reading during approval.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Reserve '-' for null/undefined/'' only: `if (v === null || v === undefined || v === '') return '-'; return Number(v).toLocaleString('en-MY', { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 })`. Apply the same to money0.

confirmed.title: No route-level code splitting — public /register applicants download the entire admin payroll bundle
confirmed.evidence: All twelve pages are statically imported (`import Login from './pages/Login.jsx'` ... `import HRCompliance from './pages/HRCompliance.jsx'`), producing one bundle. Mobile applicants on spotty connections (the PWA's stated audience) must fetch PayrollRun, Dashboard, Settings, HR pages, etc. before the registration form renders. The audit dimension and §11 bundle budget call for route-level splitting; at minimum the public face should not carry the authed app.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Convert page imports to `React.lazy(() => import('./pages/X.jsx'))` with a <Suspense fallback> — at minimum split Register (public) from the authed app so /register loads only React + router + the form. Keep the Register chunk in the SW precache so the offline form still works.

confirmed.title: UI Docker build ignores package-lock.json and uses npm install — unpinned, non-reproducible builds
confirmed.evidence: `COPY package.json ./` followed by `RUN npm install` — package-lock.json (present in ui/) is never copied, so every image build re-resolves semver ranges (react ^18.3.1, vite ^5.4.11, vite-plugin-pwa ^1.3.0) at build time. A payroll UI image can silently pick up different dependency versions between builds (supply-chain drift, unreproducible releases).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Change to `COPY package.json package-lock.json ./` and `RUN npm ci` so the lockfile is authoritative in the image build.

confirmed.title: UI served over plain HTTP with no security headers — service worker and install silently fail on any non-localhost deployment
confirmed.evidence: nginx only has `listen 80;` and docker-compose.yml publishes `"8077:80"` with no TLS termination anywhere in the stack. PRD Phase 5 hard requirement: "HTTPS ... passes Lighthouse PWA installability checks" — service workers and beforeinstallprompt require a secure context, so on any real host the SW never registers and offline drafts/queueing never activate (it only works on localhost dev). The session cookie and RESTRICTED payroll/NRIC/bank data also travel cleartext. nginx.conf additionally sets no security headers (X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, HSTS, CSP).
confirmed.proposed_fix: Terminate TLS in front of the ui container (Caddy/Traefik service in compose, or certs + `listen 443 ssl` in nginx) and document HTTPS as a deploy prerequisite in README/run.md. Add baseline headers in nginx.conf: `add_header X-Content-Type-Options nosniff; add_header X-Frame-Options DENY;` plus HSTS once TLS exists, and a CSP that also removes the need for the Tailwind CDN origin (see FE-02).

confirmed.title: One-click Deactivate on the employee list, adjacent to Edit, with no confirmation
confirmed.evidence: `<button onClick={() => toggle(e)} ...>{e.active ? 'Deactivate' : 'Activate'}</button>` fires `POST /api/employees/{id}/toggle` immediately — no confirm dialog, and the button sits directly beside the Edit link on every row. An accidental click marks an active employee inactive, silently excluding them from the next payroll run's "Add all active"/sync (an unpaid active employee violates the §1 guarantee). Contrast: run delete, approve, submit, reject and bank-verify all use window.confirm.
confirmed.proposed_fix: Wrap the deactivate direction in a confirm (`if (e.active && !window.confirm(`Deactivate ${e.name}? They will be excluded from new payroll runs.`)) return`), or replace with an explicit menu action; keep the flash-with-undo pattern as an alternative.

gaps.title: Foreign-worker and age-60 statutory branches missing: SOCSO charges foreigners Category 1, EPF ignores the 2% foreign rule and the 60+ (0%/4%) rates
gaps.evidence: compute() passes `foreign` only to eis.contribution (line 93); socso.contribution(stat, inp.over_60, inp.socso_enabled, cfg) has no foreign branch, so a foreign worker under 60 is charged employee-side Category 1 SOCSO when PERKESO puts foreign workers on the employer-only Employment Injury Scheme. kwsp.contribution(wage, enabled) is binary — no foreign rate and no age-60+ rate (citizen 60+ should be employee 0% / employer 4%; engine charges 11%/13%). The repo's own tooling asserts the rule it violates: build_payroll.py instructions sheet says 'Foreign workers (e.g. Nay Lin Zaw): SOCSO Employment-Injury applies, and EPF becomes mandatory at 2% from Oct 2025' — and Nay Lin Zaw is in the live ACTIVE_ROSTER (backend/import_legacy_form.py:38-43). Domain file .claude/domain/payroll/statutory.md H5 marks foreign EPF/SOCSO divergence [confirmed] and OPEN-2 ('who derives over_60/foreign') was never resolved. STAT-05 only covered the age-60 cutoff date for SOCSO; no STAT finding covers foreign SOCSO, foreign EPF, or 60+ EPF rates.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `foreign` to socso.contribution and route foreign workers to the Employment Injury Scheme (employer-only 1.25% table); add age/foreign parameters to kwsp.contribution implementing citizen-60+ (0%/4%) and non-citizen (2%/2% from Oct 2025) rates from the official schedules; derive both flags from DOB and identity_type at run time (resolving domain OPEN-2); extend the self-test with foreign and 60+ worked scenarios.

gaps.title: Statutory nationality inferred from bank name ('merchantrade') and EPF silently disabled for all part-time staff
gaps.evidence: _is_foreign(bank) returns True iff 'merchantrade' appears in the bank name (lines 115-117); this boolean drives EIS exclusion and epf_enabled=(employment_type=='full_time' and not foreign) at line 152. A Malaysian using Merchantrade loses EPF and EIS; a foreign worker using Maybank is treated as local. Separately, every part-time/hourly employee gets epf_enabled=False although EPF is mandatory for part-time employees (Part-Time Employees Regulations); no hr_review_flag is raised for either guess, violating the zero-silent-fixes rule. Note registration.py:127 uses the correct signal (identity_type != 'nric') — the importer diverges. No DL/STAT finding covers this classification path.
gaps.proposed_fix: Derive is_foreign from identity_type (passport/unhcr) exactly as registration.py does; never from bank name. Make part-time EPF eligibility an explicit HR decision with a warning flag instead of a hardcoded False. Raise a work_authorization_review / statutory-classification flag whenever the importer guesses either value.

gaps.title: Leavers vanish from payroll_master_view (and the master CSV the clerk pays from) the moment they resign — final month's pay is never exported
gaps.evidence: payroll_master_view has `where e.status = 'active'` (0004_views.sql:36). The resign endpoint (backend/app/hr.py:260-281) inserts the 'resigned' history row immediately, and trg_employees_status syncs employees.status = 'resigned' at once (0005_status_lifecycle.sql:60) — even when last_working_day is weeks away. So the employee drops out of the master view and master CSV instantly; the export's `last_working_day >= period start` filter (payroll_export.py:47) is dead code because resigned rows never reach it. This contradicts PRD Phase 2 ('They simply drop out of the payroll view after last_working_day') and Phase 4's view spec, and makes acceptance criterion 4 pass vacuously (ALL leavers are excluded, not just last month's). The status sync also flips the `active` boolean the run population pays from, so the final salary is dropped from the run too. No STAT/DL finding covers the premature exclusion direction.
gaps.proposed_fix: Change the view predicate to include employees whose last_working_day is null or >= the period start regardless of resigned/terminated status (status in ('active') OR (status in ('resigned','terminated','absconded') and last_working_day >= period start)), parameterized via the export query; add the PRD's acceptance test in both directions (leaver last month excluded, leaver this month included with final_pay_due).

gaps.title: rls_test.sql proves almost nothing: 4 of 14 tables, no views, no staff/manager cases, no assertions — yet README cites it as proof
gaps.evidence: The script tests only employees, bank_accounts, pay_profiles, employee_documents as anon, and two tables as authenticated. It never touches payslips, payroll_runs, users (password hashes), settings, audit_log, hr_review_flags, emergency_contacts, application_submissions, employee_status_history, employee_positions — all RLS-enabled in 0003_rls.sql:8-21 — and never queries payroll_master_view/payroll_blocked_view/payroll_movements_view, the exact security-definer leak SEC-02 confirmed. It has no assertions ('Every SELECT must return 0 rows' is an eyeball instruction), so it cannot fail in CI, and there is no recorded run output. PRD acceptance criterion 2 explicitly requires proving 'staff cannot read others' bank rows' — impossible since no staff role exists. README.md:57 nevertheless claims RLS is 'proven by supabase/rls_test.sql'.
gaps.proposed_fix: Rewrite as an asserting script (DO blocks raising exceptions on any visible row / permitted write) covering every RLS table and all three views for anon and authenticated; add staff/manager cases once those roles exist (GAP-05); wire it into `make test` and record a passing run; soften the README claim until it actually passes.

gaps.title: PRD role model unimplemented: no staff self-service role, no outlet-scoped manager role, no per-role RLS policies
gaps.evidence: PRD Phase 1 requires four RLS roles: hr_admin (full), manager (outlet-scoped employee reads, no bank/pay/identity docs), staff (read/update own contact fields, upload own documents), anon (insert-only submissions). The app implements only preparer/approver/admin API-level guards (security.py role checks); 0003_rls.sql is deny-all with no per-role policies; there is no employee login, no self-service contact update, no own-document upload, and no outlet scoping anywhere in backend or ui/src. Existing SEC findings cover auth weaknesses of the roles that exist, but no dimension flagged that two of the PRD's four roles were never built.
gaps.proposed_fix: Either implement staff self-service (own-record contact edit + document upload behind employee auth) and outlet-scoped manager reads with matching RLS policies, or record a human DECISION descoping them from Payroll 2.0 and update README/PRD traceability accordingly.

gaps.title: HR 'request re-submission' action (PRD Phase 5B) does not exist in backend or UI
gaps.evidence: PRD Phase 5B lists HR actions: 'resolve/dismiss flags, request re-submission, edit fields (audited), Approve, Reject'. grep for resubmit/re_submit/resubmission across backend/ and ui/src returns nothing; hr.py exposes approve, reject, resign, flag resolve/dismiss, edits — but no way to ask an applicant to fix or re-send a bad submission (wrong NRIC photo, corrupted bank account). HR's only options for a fixable submission are rejecting it outright or editing data themselves, which defeats the verification intent for bank/NRIC corrections.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a request-resubmission endpoint + UI action that sets a distinct employee state or flag, issues a re-entry link/reference for the public form pre-keyed to the existing record, and audits the request; surface it in the HR queue.

gaps.title: Uninventoried PII surfaces: real names, full bank account numbers and salaries hardcoded in build_payroll.py, plus seven git-tracked data files no SEC/INFRA finding names
gaps.evidence: build_payroll.py:317+ hardcodes the real roster with full bank account numbers and salaries (e.g. emp("ON00010", "cheong fong cheng", "Cimb", "7000986177", ..., basic=5000)). JUNE_2026_PAYROLL_ANALYSIS.md contains real employee names with payroll figures. backend/import_legacy_form.py:38-43 hardcodes the ACTIVE_ROSTER real names (SEC-09 named only seed.py). git ls-files confirms these tracked PII files that no SEC/INFRA finding enumerates: emp_payroll_2605.xlsx, emp_payroll_2606.xlsx, 'employee-registration-form (1).xlsx' (root), 2607/Emp_Payroll_July_2026_from_img.xlsx, 2607/emp_payroll_2607._populated.backup.xlsx (+2 .bak variants), backups/pre-migration-20260802.sql, backups/payroll.db.20260802, webapp/payroll.db. SEC-08/SEC-09/INFRA-08 covered only the backend image xlsx, seed.py names, and the Sheet ID; worklog ERR-001 flags the class of problem but the audit produced no complete remediation inventory and .gitignore excludes none of these.
gaps.proposed_fix: Treat this list plus SEC-08/09/INFRA-08 items as the canonical PII purge inventory: replace hardcoded rosters/accounts in build_payroll.py and import_legacy_form.py with external synthetic fixtures, delete or externalize the xlsx/db/sql data files, add exclusion patterns to .gitignore, then execute the human-approved git-history rewrite ERR-001 is waiting on.

gaps.title: PRD deliverables never produced or verified: Phase 0 discovery report absent, no deployment/Lighthouse/airplane-mode verification, daily expiry job a silent no-op without pg_cron
gaps.evidence: Deliverable 1 (Phase 0 discovery report before any migration) exists nowhere in the repo (grep across docs/, .claude/, *.md finds nothing). Deliverable 5's verification steps were never executed: no deployment exists (FE-11 covers HTTP but not the missing deployment/Lighthouse run), and the offline form-draft airplane-mode check was never performed or recorded. Deliverable 4's resigned-employee check was never run as a test — and would currently mask GAP-03 since it only tests the exclusion direction. Phase 2's 'daily' expiry job is scheduled only `if exists pg_cron` (0005_status_lifecycle.sql:106-111); the compose postgres:16 image has no pg_cron and the local profile never applies migrations (INFRA-03), so on every non-Supabase deployment flags refresh only at backend startup (main.py:49) and compliance-board loads (hr.py:348) — never daily.
gaps.proposed_fix: Write the discovery report retroactively into docs/; add an acceptance-criteria traceability checklist mapping each PRD deliverable to evidence (test, run log, or DECISION descoping it); run and record Lighthouse + offline-draft verification once FE-01/FE-02 are fixed; make expiry-flag freshness deterministic (in-app scheduler or documented cron) instead of the conditional pg_cron block.

gaps.title: Documentation asserts things the code contradicts; mandated worklog is skeletal
gaps.evidence: README.md:57 claims RLS is 'proven by supabase/rls_test.sql' (contradicted by GAP-04/SEC-02); README.md:97-98 claims import 're-runs refresh satellite rows and never duplicate' while DL-05 shows re-runs delete HR-verified bank rows, documents, and append-only history; README.md:16 and run.md:13 publish the weak demo credentials (SEC-03). README_PAYROLL.md claims SOCSO uses the 'Official RM100-band table' though the engine formula deviates at 5-sen ties (domain H1) and the band table misses sub-bands (STAT-06); JUNE_2026_PAYROLL_ANALYSIS.md opens with 'All figures verified' against an engine now shown wrong (STAT-01/02/06, GAP-01), and states SOCSO Cat 1 employee 0.5% while the live engine constant is 1.25% (QT-02). docs/worklog.md has zero FIX/LL rows and no session summaries despite CLAUDE.md Part 4 making them mandatory.
gaps.proposed_fix: Correct or caveat each claim as the referenced fixes land (treat README as part of every fix's definition of done); mark JUNE_2026_PAYROLL_ANALYSIS.md as superseded; backfill worklog fixes/lessons/session-summary sections when the audit remediation begins.

gaps.title: OT-eligibility fallback hardcodes the RM4,000 rule as logic in payroll_master_view, which the PRD explicitly forbade
gaps.evidence: The view computes `coalesce(pp.ot_eligible, e.basic_salary <= 4000)` — a statutory-coverage rule baked into SQL. The PRD's pay_profiles spec says 'statutory OT applies ≤ RM4,000/month basic — verify current rule, don't hardcode as logic' (ot_eligible is meant to be an HR-set boolean). The fallback also reads legacy employees.basic_salary (RM numeric) rather than pay_profiles sen, silently deciding OT eligibility for every employee whose pay_profile row is missing — which per DL-08 is most of them, since pay_profiles is write-only.
gaps.proposed_fix: Remove the salary-threshold fallback from the view; make ot_eligible NOT NULL on pay_profiles set explicitly at HR activation, and raise a review flag instead of guessing when it is absent. Keep any statutory threshold in the rates config with a verification note, not in DDL.
